'''Vesselin Atanasov Dimitrov''' (in Bulgarian: ''Веселин Атанасов Димитров'') is a [[Bulgaria|Bulgarian]] mathematician known for his work in [[arithmetic geometry]], [[Diophantine geometry]], [[modular form]]s and [[number theory]]. He is currently a professor at [[California Institute of Technology|Caltech]], having previously taught at the [[University of Toronto]].

Dimitrov received the [[Oberwolfach Prize]] and the [[Journal of Number Theory#David Goss prize|David Goss Prize]] in 2022. In 2025, he received the [[Salem Prize]] and the [[Fermat Prize]], and in 2026, the [[Frank Nelson Cole Prize|Cole Prize]] in Number Theory.

==Research in mathematics==
In 2019 Dimitrov proved the [[Schinzel–Zassenhaus conjecture]] on algebraic units that are not roots of unity.<ref>{{cite book |last1=McKee |first1=James |chapter=The Schinzel–Zassenhaus conjecture |year=2021 |title=Around the Unit Circle: Mahler Measure, Integer Matrices and Roots of Unity |pages=69–75 |place=[[Cham, Switzerland|Cham]] |publisher=[[Springer-Verlag|Springer]] |doi=10.1007/978-3-030-80031-4_4 |isbn=978-3-030-80030-7 |last2=Smyth |first2=Chris}}</ref><ref name=":0"/><ref>{{cite arXiv |last=Dimitrov |first=Vesselin |title=A proof of the Schinzel-Zassenhaus conjecture on polynomials |date=2019-12-28 |class=math.NT |eprint=1912.12545}}</ref>
 
Together with [[Ziyang Gao]] and [[Philipp Habegger]], he proved a uniform version of the [[Mordell conjecture]].<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dimitrov |first1=Vesselin |last2=Gao |first2=Ziyang |last3=Habegger |first3=Philipp |author3-link=Philipp Habegger |year=2021 |title=Uniformity in Mordell–Lang for curves |journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]] |volume=194 |issue=1 |doi=10.4007/annals.2021.194.1.4 |mr=4276287 |pages=237-298|arxiv=2001.10276 }}</ref>

In collaboration with [[Frank Calegari]] and [[Yunqing Tang]], Dimitrov proved the unbounded denominators conjecture of [[A. O. L. Atkin|Atkin]] and [[Peter Swinnerton-Dyer|Swinnerton-Dyer]]: if a modular form {{tmath|f(\tau)}} is not modular for some [[congruence subgroup]] of the [[modular group]], then the Fourier coefficients of {{tmath|f(\tau)}} have unbounded denominators.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Calegari |first1=Frank |author1-link=Frank Calegari |last2=Dimitrov |first2=Vesselin |last3=Tang |first3=Yunqing |author3-link=Yunqing Tang |date=2025 |title=The unbounded denominators conjecture |journal=[[Journal of the American Mathematical Society]] |language=en |volume=38 |issue=3 |pages=627–702 |doi=10.1090/jams/1053}}</ref>

==Early life and education==

In 2005, he won a silver medal in the [[International Mathematics Olympiad]], representing Bulgaria.<ref>[[International Mathematics Olympiad]] web-site: [https://www.imo-official.org/team_r.aspx?code=BGR&year=2005 Bulgaria 2005]</ref>

He earned a PhD from [[Yale University]] in 2017 under the supervision of [[Alexander Goncharov]]. His thesis is titled "Diophantine approximations by special points and applications to Dynamics and Geometry".<ref>{{MathGenealogy|250763}}</ref>

==Awards==
Dimitrov's work has been recognized by the following awards:
*2022: [[Journal of Number Theory#David Goss prize|David Goss Prize]] (shared with Ziyang Gao)<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/202210/rnoti-p1829.pdf|title=Dimitrov and Gao Awarded 2022 David Goss Prize|journal=[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]]|pages=1832–1833|volume=69|issue=10|year=2022}}</ref>; [[Oberwolfach Research Institute for Mathematics#Oberwolfach Prize|Oberwolfach Prize]]<ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=https://www.mfo.de/outreach-media/prizes/oberwolfach-prize/laudationdimitrovoberwolfachfin.pdf|first=Jean-Benoît|last=Bost|title=Oberwolfach Prize 2022 Laudatio for Vesselin Dimitrov|publisher=Oberwolfach Research Institute for Mathematics}}</ref>
*2023: IMI Mathematics Prize (Institute of Mathematics and Informatics, Bulgarian Academy of Sciences)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://math.gatech.edu/news/richard-duke-assistant-professor-vesselin-dimitrov-laureate-2023-imi-mathematics-prize|title=Richard A. Duke Assistant Professor Vesselin Dimitrov is the laureate of the 2023 IMI Mathematics Prize|publisher=Georgia Tech|date=September 4, 2023}}</ref>
*2025: [[Salem Prize]], "for fundamental contributions to Diophantine geometry and number theory";<ref name="Salem">{{cite web|url=https://www.ias.edu/math/2025-salem-prize-winners|title=2025 Salem Prize Winners - School of Mathematics &#124; Institute for Advanced Study|date=October 27, 2025|website=www.ias.edu}}</ref> [[Fermat Prize]].<ref>''[[Institut de Mathématiques de Toulouse]]'': [https://euromathsoc.org/news/2025-fermat-prize-awarded-to-vesselin-dimitrov-and-vlad-vicol-191 Fermat Prize 2025]</ref>
*2026: [[Breakthrough Prize in Mathematics#New Horizons in Mathematics Prize|New Horizons in Mathematics Prize]] (shared with [[Yunqing Tang]]); [[Frank Nelson Cole Prize|Cole Prize]] in Number Theory (shared with [[Frank Calegari]] and Yunqing Tang), for their paper "The unbounded denominators conjecture".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/news?news_id=7548|title=Calegari, Dimitrov, and Tang to Receive 2026 AMS Frank Nelson Cole Prize for Number Theory|website=www.ams.org|access-date=25 July 2026}}</ref>
